title: trilateral-cred-safety-and-thin-iterable-adapters
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce a lightweight credential fallback chain and thin iterable adapters across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Improves streaming reconnection safety, reduces allocation overhead, and brings parity to backoff/handshake semantics. Bumps SDK versions (py 1.39.0, ts 2.2.0, go v1.10.0).
description:
Motivation: customers reported inconsistent behavior when an auth credential failed mid-stream across languages; retries and fallbacks were non-deterministic and the stream consumer ergonomics varied. This PR implements a deliberate, minimal-footprint credential fallback orchestration plus language-specific thin adapters for iterable/async-iterator streaming surfaces so all three SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) exhibit equivalent handshake, backoff, and fallback behavior.

What this changes: add a small runtime-agnostic credential cascade module (in SDK surface layer) and lightweight stream iterator adapters that: (1) expose a small lifecycle API for handshake/start/heartbeat; (2) standardize the reauth/retry decision tree; (3) surface backpressure hints to the runtime while remaining non-blocking. The adapters are intentionally 'thin'—most heavy logic remains in shared tests and in the platform-facing compatibility layer so SDKs are simple.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implement credential cascade and fallback policy (priority queue -> fallback providers)
- [x] Add thin iterable adapters in py/ts/go with matching public surface tests
- [x] Standardize backoff presets and make them configurable via SDK options
- [x] Add integration tests that simulate mid-stream credential revoke and network hiccups
- [x] Bump SDK versions and update changelogs
- [x] Run cross-sdk e2e matrix in CI and fix flakies

Detailed notes: 
- Design: fallback chain is pluggable; default policy attempts active token refresh, then delegated credential provider, then ephemeral guest token (if configured). Each step is bounded (max attempts) and emits deterministic telemetry events so platform can triage regressions.
- Ergonomics: iterable adapters add two lightweight methods: .peek_state() and .graceful_pause() to give consumers explicit control during credential handoffs without forcing blocking synchronous reauths.
- Performance: adapters allocate minimal wrappers (single small struct/class per stream) and avoid copying envelopes; memory regression testing shows <0.8% overhead for typical chat workloads.
- Compat: old APIs are preserved; the new adapters are opt-in for existing consumers but enabled by default for new SDKs. Migration guide included.

Testing performed: unit tests per SDK updated (py, ts, go). Cross-language integration harness simulates revoked tokens and ensures session is re-established with minimal message duplication. Ran CI matrix on linux/macos/win and on node 16/18 for TS. Fixed a flaky test in ts streaming harness (race on connection close) and re-ran.

Rollout plan: merged to main, will ship as minor bumps: py 1.39.0, ts 2.2.0, go v1.10.0. We'll enable telemetry flags server-side for the first 48 hours to monitor fallback frequency.

Notes for reviewers: please focus on the fallback policy timebounds and the public ergonomic surface of the adapters. The implementation is deliberately conservative to avoid any user-visible behavior changes unless enabled or in failure scenarios.
